    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      id-token: write # the decision signature, nothing else
      attestations: write # store the decision in the caller's attestation store
    env:
      SBOM_RESULT: ${{ needs.sbom.result }}
      REPRO_RESULT: ${{ needs.repro-gate.result }}
    steps:
      - name: Refuse unless every required proof succeeded
        env:
          UNTRUSTED_CLASSES: ${{ inputs.classes }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          proofs='[]'
          for p in "sbom and advisory triage:${SBOM_RESULT}" "repro gate:${REPRO_RESULT}"; do
            name="${p%:*}" result="${p##*:}"
            proofs=$(jq -c --arg n "${name}" --arg r "${result}" \
              '. + [{name: $n, result: $r}]' <<< "${proofs}")
            if [[ ${result} != "success" ]]; then
              echo "::error::${name} is '${result}' — absence of a proof is never a proof"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          ((fail == 0)) || exit 1
          # The decision predicate: every proof by name, its conclusion,
          # the tag and the classes — assembled HERE, in the job that
          # holds the results, so the claim is the check's return value.
          decided_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
          jq -n \
            --arg tag "v${VERSION}" \
            --arg classes "${UNTRUSTED_CLASSES}" \
            --arg at "${decided_at}" \
            --argjson proofs "${proofs}" \
            '{tag: $tag, classes: $classes, conclusion: "OPEN",
              decidedAt: $at, proofs: $proofs}' \
            > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/decision-predicate.json"
          echo "::notice::commit point open: every required proof succeeded"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-sbom
          path: sbom-subject

      - name: Stage the decision subjects (the inventory the decision covered)
        env:
          INVENTORY: ${{ matrix.inventory }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/decision-subjects.sha256"
          if [[ -n ${INVENTORY} ]]; then
            # A planned inventory decides for itself and names nothing
            # else. Resolved by listing, never by building a path out of
            # the matrix value.
            found=""
            listing=$(find sbom-subject -type f | sort)
            while IFS= read -r f; do
              [[ -n ${f} ]] || continue
              name=$(basename "${f}")
              if [[ ${name} == "${INVENTORY}" ]]; then found="${f}"; fi
            done <<< "${listing}"
            [[ -n ${found} ]] || {
              echo "::error::the plan names ${INVENTORY} but the sbom artifact does not carry it"
              exit 1
            }
            files="${found}"
          else
            # No plan: one decision over the whole release, the
            # invariant every pre-inventory release shipped under.
            files=$(find sbom-subject -type f | sort)
          fi
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            [[ -n ${f} ]] || continue
            digest=$(sha256sum "${f}" | cut -d' ' -f1)
            base=$(basename "${f}")
            printf '%s  %s\n' "${digest}" "${base}" \
              >> "${RUNNER_TEMP}/decision-subjects.sha256"
          done <<< "${files}"
          [[ -s "${RUNNER_TEMP}/decision-subjects.sha256" ]] || {
            echo "::error::the sbom artifact is empty — a decision over nothing decides nothing"
            exit 1
          }
      - name: Sign the decision under this workflow's identity
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ${{ runner.temp }}/decision-subjects.sha256
          predicate-type: https://monumental-archive.github.io/attestations/release-decision/v1
          predicate-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/decision-predicate.json

  # Last, and only on proof. Attaches the evidence bundle and publishes the
  # draft — the first moment anything becomes public.
  #
  # Fan-in, by construction: `needs` names every PROVENANCE sign job, the
  # `if` demands that nothing upstream failed AND that every REQUESTED
  # class delivered its signature (dry-run excuses the classes whose
  # signer legitimately skipped). A skipped class never blocks; a failed
  # or missing one always does. The VSA jobs are deliberately absent:
  # verdicts run AFTER this job, against the published immutable release
  # (#209) — attach publishes on evidence, verdicts follow. Assets and
  # bundles travel as `release-*` / `attestation-bundle-*` artifacts, so
  # the BYTES need no per-class input.
  #
  # Their LEG does — its class since stele#185 and its target since
  # stele#223: `stele emit manifest` requires every build subject to be
  # claimed by exactly one (class, target), and the fan-in's
  # `merge-multiple` erases the class the artifact name carried while
  # nothing ever carried the target. So each build leg's own subject
  # manifest — the same digests its signer signs, one target column
  # wider — rides down as a per-class input. The leg-to-class
  # map is already stated twice in this job (the `if` names both halves
  # of every pair); this is the third use of the same map, in the file
  # that holds it, rather than a second map derived from artifact names
  # in the callee. A new class is one more job above, one `if` clause,
  # and one forwarded input.
  #
  # oci-image and wasm-npm forward nothing: they publish to a registry
  # and attach no release asset, so they own no build subject and
  # passing their build outputs REFUSES.
  # phase: attest
  attach:
    name: Attach evidence and publish
    needs:
      - guard
      - sbom
      - sign
      - sign-image
      - sign-binaries
      - sign-go
      - sign-source
      - sign-wasm
      - sign-extensions
      - sign-extension-images
      # The build legs join `needs` only to bring their subject
      # manifests into scope. Each is already an ancestor through its
      # sign job, so no ordering changes and no `if` clause moves: a
      # failed build already failed its signer, and a skipped one
      # contributes `skipped`, which the failure test below ignores.
      - build
      - build-binary
      - build-go
      - build-source
      - build-extension
      # And the three that publish to a registry, for the same reason
      # and under the same argument: each is already an ancestor
      # through its signer.
      - assemble-oci
      - build-wasm
      - build-extension-images
    if: >-
      ${{
        !cancelled() && needs.guard.result == 'success'
        && needs.sbom.result == 'success'
        && !contains(join(needs.*.result, ','), 'failure')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'rust-crate') || needs.sign.result == 'success')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'oci-image') || needs.sign-image.result == 'success' || inputs.dry-run)
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'rust-binary') || needs.sign-binaries.result == 'success')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'go-binary') || needs.sign-go.result == 'success')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'source-archive') || needs.sign-source.result == 'success')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'wasm-npm') || needs.sign-wasm.result == 'success')
        && (!contains(inputs.classes, 'pgrx-extension')
          || (needs.sign-extensions.result == 'success'
            && (needs.sign-extension-images.result == 'success' || inputs.dry-run)))
      }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/attach-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions: {} # it publishes with the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
      # The manifest is written where the release's assets ALL exist,
      # which is this job and nowhere earlier (stele#156). The classes
      # ride with it because the manifest declares them; it is one
      # string, not the per-class inputs this fan-in deliberately has
      # none of.
      #
      # The guard's derived list, not the caller's raw one (#843): the
      # manifest declares what the release OWES, and a crate-built image
      # owes an inventory a Dockerfile-only one does not. The same
      # string reached the plans judgment before the commit point, so
      # the pre-publish check and the evidence walk read one obligation
      # list from one derivation.
      classes: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.classes }}
      # One line per artifact of every class that attaches release
      # assets, each carrying the target its leg built, empty when that
      # class did not run. The flat `subjects` output stays what the
      # signers take; this is the same digests plus the one column only
      # the leg holds.
      rust-crate-leg-subjects: ${{ needs.build.outputs.leg-subjects }}
      rust-binary-leg-subjects: ${{ needs.build-binary.outputs.leg-subjects }}
      go-binary-leg-subjects: ${{ needs.build-go.outputs.leg-subjects }}
      source-archive-leg-subjects: ${{ needs.build-source.outputs.leg-subjects }}
      pgrx-extension-leg-subjects: ${{ needs.build-extension.outputs.leg-subjects }}
      # What each registry class published there, which no asset can
      # say (#1168). A rehearsal publishes to no registry, so it claims
      # nothing: the image index is not assembled on a dry run and its
      # output is already empty, while the tarball and the per-major
      # indexes are BUILT on one and must be withheld here.
      oci-image-registry-subjects: ${{ needs.assemble-oci.outputs.registry-subjects }}
      oci-image-class: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.image-class || 'oci-image' }}
      wasm-npm-registry-subjects: ${{ !inputs.dry-run && needs.build-wasm.outputs.registry-subjects || '' }}
      pgrx-extension-image-registry-subjects: >-
        ${{ !inputs.dry-run && needs.build-extension-images.outputs.registry-subjects || '' }}
      pgrx-extension-image-class: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.extension-image-class }}
      dry-run: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
    secrets:
      app-private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}

  # The release-asset verdicts: binaries, source archives and extension
  # tarballs became public URLs the moment attach published, and immutable
  # at the same moment — so their first pull-back is here, post-publish,
  # against exactly the bytes a stranger fetches. Subjects come from the
  # build (what the signer attested); the verdict job re-proves every one
  # against the release before opening any evidence. See the note on
  # `vsa` above for the pattern; the VSA is signed over the verdict job's
  # own re-proved manifest.
  # phase: attest
  vsa-binaries:
    name: Assemble and sign binaries VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - build-binary
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'rust-binary') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # pull-back plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      subjects: ${{ needs.build-binary.outputs.subjects }}
      release-tag: ${{ format('v{0}', needs.guard.outputs.version) }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}

  # phase: attest
  vsa-go:
    name: Assemble and sign Go binaries VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - build-go
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'go-binary') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # pull-back plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      subjects: ${{ needs.build-go.outputs.subjects }}
      release-tag: ${{ format('v{0}', needs.guard.outputs.version) }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}

  # phase: attest
  vsa-source:
    name: Assemble and sign source VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - build-source
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'source-archive') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # pull-back plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      subjects: ${{ needs.build-source.outputs.subjects }}
      release-tag: ${{ format('v{0}', needs.guard.outputs.version) }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}

  # phase: attest
  vsa-extensions:
    name: Assemble and sign extensions VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - build-extension
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'pgrx-extension') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # pull-back plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      subjects: ${{ needs.build-extension.outputs.subjects }}
      release-tag: ${{ format('v{0}', needs.guard.outputs.version) }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
      # File subjects, but built INSIDE the pinned postgres base set —
      # the one class where subject shape and base-image consumption
      # disagree (#310 finding 4). The claim is per-major: exactly the
      # mapping rows the build matrix instantiated (#316 finding 3).
      base-majors: ${{ inputs.pg-majors }}

  # The image verdicts. No pull-back — content addressing already proves
  # the bytes; what the verdict job proves is the mutable half, that the
  # tag the release advertises resolves in the registry to the attested
  # index digest, and then opens the provenance oci:// at that digest.
  # One verdict covers the class's whole image set (a subject line per
  # index), signed over the verdict job's re-proved manifest exactly like
  # the file classes — the subject names are the untagged references the
  # signer attested.
  # phase: attest
  vsa-image:
    name: Assemble and sign image VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - assemble-oci
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'oci-image') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # pull-back plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      images: >-
        ${{ format('[{{"image":"{0}","tag":"{1}","digest":"{2}"}}]',
        needs.assemble-oci.outputs.image, needs.guard.outputs.version,
        needs.assemble-oci.outputs.digest) }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
      # No base-majors: the oci-image class is FROM scratch — a
      # musl-static binary in an empty image has no base layer, and the
      # enrichment claims nothing it did not consume (#316 finding 3).

  # phase: attest
  vsa-extension-images:
    name: Assemble and sign extension images VSA
    needs:
      - sbom
      - guard
      - build-extension-images
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && contains(inputs.classes, 'pgrx-extension') && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify-release.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # registry resolution plus attestation reads
      id-token: write # the verdict signs itself — verifier.id IS the certificate (#264)
      attestations: write # persist the verdict in the store
      artifact-metadata: write # the attestation storage record
    with:
      mode: verdict
      inventories: ${{ needs.sbom.outputs.inventories }}
      # The signing matrix as-is: {pg, image, tag, digest} — the verdict
      # job reads image, tag and digest and ignores the rest.
      images: ${{ needs.build-extension-images.outputs.images }}
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
      # No base-majors: the extension images are FROM scratch + COPY of
      # the already-built tarballs — the base consumption happened in the
      # tarball build and is claimed on THAT class's verdict, not here
      # (#316 finding 3).

  # The DOI comes last of all: it cites a release that is already public,
  # proven and signed. Skipped on dry-run (a rehearsal must cite nothing).
  # phase: attest
  doi:
    name: Mint the version DOI
    needs:
      - guard
      - attach
    # !cancelled() + explicit attach check: the implicit success() looks
    # THROUGH attach to its legitimately-skipped class ancestors and goes
    # false — the same transitive quirk attach's own condition exists for.
    # Measured on v0.14.2, where everything succeeded and doi skipped.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.attach.result == 'success' && inputs.mint-doi && !inputs.dry-run }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/mint-doi.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
    permissions:
      contents: read # the minting job downloads the released source
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.version }}
    secrets:
      zenodo-token: ${{ secrets.zenodo-token }}

  # A tag is immutable, so a publish that dies spends its version number
  # and leaves the draft `release/tag-release.sh` cut sitting there — the
  # release correctly burned, the residue outside the taxonomy. Nothing
  # cleaned it up and nothing noticed: the evidence walk, the tag walk
  # and `derive vex-subjects` all enumerate NON-DRAFT releases and
  # `gh release view` with no tag returns the latest PUBLISHED one, so a
  # draft is invisible to every judgment in the org — by coincidence of
  # how those enumerations are written, and now stated in
  # docs/release.md rather than relied on unsaid. What a draft does
  # reach is a human reading the releases page, and at thirty-two of
  # them "burn or release in flight?" could not be answered by looking.
  #
  # So the draft becomes the record. Deleting it was the old instruction
  # and is rejected: it destroys the only artifact of the failed attempt
  # other than run logs, which expire at 90 days, and this org derives
  # burns from run history (#597).
  #
  # `needs.attach.result != 'success'` covers every way the release
  # failed to go public in ONE edge — attach failed, or attach never ran
  # because something upstream did — so a class added above wires itself
  # in rather than being silently unwatched. The `record` phase is
  # terminal by construction (`lint:release-phases`): it signs nothing,
  # publishes nothing, and nothing may depend on it, so it cannot become
  # a route around the commit point.
  # phase: record
  burn-record:
    name: Record the burn on the draft
    needs:
      - guard
      - attach
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.guard.result == 'success' && needs.attach.result != 'success' && !inputs.dry-run }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {} # it annotates with the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN
    steps:
      # No checkout: the canon action links the tree this run already
      # resolved, so the failure path costs one symlink and no network.
      - name: Resolve the canon tree (the ref the caller pinned)
        uses: $/.github/actions/canon

      - name: Mint the annotating token
        id: token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAG_MINT_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Record the burn
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          KIND: burn
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: .org-canon/release/record-draft.sh
...
